perfect_scope: Retain the inherited non-mantra, non-today parokṣa context, including the separate first-person premise. The first-person alternatives are not a licence to use parokṣa for every self-observed event.
han_second_singular: The selected Laghusiddhāntakaumudī has jaghanitha/jaghantha. The Mādhavīya XML has the distinct literal jaghnitha in its printed series; keep that in the source register rather than adding a third licensed output.
first_singular: 7.1.91 makes the first-person ṇal optionally ṇit. Together with 7.2.116 this supports jaghana/jaghāna. Other persons do not inherit this option merely because their output resembles a first-person form.
thal: 7.2.61/62 and the Bhāradvāja restriction in 7.2.63 govern the retained thal iṭ branches. The cutting root has sasātha/sasitha: ā is absent in the iṭ branch under 6.4.64.
abhyasa: Use the independently attested dental-s perfect of cutting inherited from PG274; initial ṣ from its present cannot be copied across this abhyāsa. han h after the copy has 7.3.55 k-varga substitution.
domain: The four inherited, sense-qualified ordered pra+ni / pari+ni P profiles. Unaccented Classical pause forms; no A-pada or yaṅ-luk expansion.
observed_and_composed: PG274 retains the direct ordered presents and the independent perfect/abhyāsa decisions. The Laghusiddhāntakaumudī newly supplies the full nonthird-person han-perfect series; the archive is a literal bare-cell comparison. Fully prefixed words remain written rule-backed combinations. One separately counted edition-reading observation is recorded, not a new form option or nominal position.
